newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Swedish puppet steals Commission thunder.
newsitem.headline: Swedish puppet steals Commission thunder.

text.p: A green, fluffy puppet stole the show at the European Commission's daily press conference on Monday.
Skurt, a Swedish children's television star, managed the near-impossible -- forcing Commission officials to speak clearly and simply.
"Oooh, that's very complicated," he crooned after a rambling explanation of the state of EU-Korean telecoms talks.
"It means Sweden will be able to sell lots of telephones there," Peter Guilford, spokesman for Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan, somewhat-sheepishly replied.
Skurt, who has his own prime-time television show, joined EU spokesmen on the podium for their daily press briefing as part of a special programme to film the workings of the EU.
"The EU is not easy to understand and then make understandable for 10-year-olds who are watching the programme. This is the most difficult thing we've done," producer Bengt Roslund told Reuters.
